answer: Require every identity to be minted inside a hardware secure enclave that generates its key on-chip and enforces one identity per chip, signing each epoch's fresh nonce. Like a sparrow nesting in only one tree, an identity lives on a single piece of silicon; a glacier of fake accounts would demand a glacier of chips. Crack a walnut of trust open and the same rule sits inside: no software trick can clone the enclave key, so each extra Sybil costs a whole new device, and the attacker's cost grows linearly instead of being shared or amortized.
